conditional_signature357_impact.assumption: the candidate conditional proof of primitive signature (3,5,7) is correct
conditional_signature357_impact.proof_of_minimality: enumerate sorted odd-prime triples of sum <19; FLT, the solved (3,3,n), the solved (n,n,3), the solved (5,5,7), and the solved (7,7,5) families cover every entry once (3,5,7) is assumed

nonclaim: This certificate proves a global reduction of the exponent space and identifies the next finite frontier. It does not eliminate either infinite odd-prime core and therefore does not prove the Beal conjecture.

prime_core_partition.equal_exponents: p=p=p, excluded by Fermat's Last Theorem
prime_core_partition.three_distinct_exponents: signatures (p,q,r) with distinct odd primes, an infinite open core
prime_core_partition.two_equal_exponents: signatures (p,p,q), with several solved subfamilies but an infinite open core

prime_or_special_reduction.beal_consequence: every primitive Beal counterexample has three prime exponents; because all exponents are at least 3, they are odd primes
prime_or_special_reduction.coefficient_one_beal_status: all special signatures with minimum exponent at least 3 are solved and have no primitive positive solutions
prime_or_special_reduction.source_statement: Ratcliffe--Grechuk classify every minimal non-all-prime hyperbolic signature as a special triple and state that only (2,5,9) and (2,3,25) remain open among coefficient-one non-all-prime signatures

required_uniform_breakthrough.contractive_criterion: a theorem excluding sorted prime signatures p<=q<=r whenever r>B(p,q), with B(p,q)<q outside a finite boundary, would eliminate the entire cofinal distinct-prime region
required_uniform_breakthrough.statement: isolated signature proofs cannot terminate the global problem; one needs an infinite-family theorem covering the repeated-prime core and a cofinal region of the three-distinct-prime core

source_dependencies.signature357: candidate conditional research proof in Research/Signature357; not treated as a peer-reviewed theorem by this certificate

relevant_items: the statement that only (2,5,9) and (2,3,25) remain among non-all-prime coefficient-one signatures
survey.title: Generalised Fermat equation: a survey of solved cases

unconditional_canonical_reduction.existence_proof: If n is odd, any prime divisor of n is odd. If n is even and 4 does not divide n, write n=2m with odd m>=3 and choose an odd prime divisor of m.
unconditional_canonical_reduction.primitivity_preservation: a prime dividing powers of two original pairwise-coprime bases would divide both original bases

rule.reduced_exponent: an odd prime p dividing n
